video_title_guess: LeBron James Breaks Down Round 1 of the 2026 NBA Playoffs

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: I definitely didn't believe that. I mean, listen, I came to the Lakers in 2018 at 33. And there's no way if if someone were to say, would you be playing in 2026 in the postseason, like, you know, just playing. Like, I I don't know if I would have been able to answer that question, just playing. And then let alone saying, hey, now, but now you're the number one option on a playoff team and you're helping to win a series. Like, you're the number one option on that team. I just I wouldn't have believed it. I mean, you know, I knew I still had a lot left in the tank when I came to this franchise in 18, but to say that, you know, eight years later, you know, at 41, I would be leading a team into the postseason and and and and then, you know, coming out with a with a series win. Um I I wouldn't have guessed that and I and I wouldn't have bet on that.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron expresses surprise at his continued dominance and role as the primary option at 41, highlighting his unprecedented longevity and impact in the league.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: I felt like I had to start with our preparation and our belief. You know, at the end of the day, you know, it doesn't matter what the bookmakers are saying or, you know, the experts, so-called experts are saying, the game is always won in between the four lines and we had to prepare. And obviously, we know we were going against, you know, you know, different circumstances and and against the odds, obviously, without Luka, without AR to start the series and, um, you know, them being, you know, super well-equipped and and and ready for whatever, um, you know, that we would bring to the table. But the game is, like I said, this game is always won in between the four lines. If we could prepare ourself, um, you know, um, and you know, we could play well, um, we could compete at a high level, we could bring the physicality that Houston brought to the table, uh, then we felt like we had a good chance of of of trying to, you know, win each game. And that's all that mattered. It wasn't about the series. We was like, how can we win one game at a time, you know, and I think we started building confidence and guys just played well and, uh, you know, we were able to to win it in in six versus a, you know, a very good team.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron emphasizes the importance of internal preparation and belief over external predictions, especially when facing adversity and missing key players in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: I kind of I've always like always been locked in. That moment right there, throwing him the lob, seeing him make the three, we kind of going back and forth. I kind of blanked out for a little bit and just like really just accepted it and and and relished in that moment. And that's pretty cool for for for me as a dad and then us as as colleagues and and then our whole family. Like, I think I mentioned at one point like my mom being at the game and her being able to watch her son and grandson in the postseason game at the same time. Like, you know, and it's the same. My wife was there. Yeah, my wife was there, his sister was there. I think Bryce was back home from college. He was at the playoff. Like it was like, you can't you can't even, you know, you can't even write that script in Hollywood better than than than what's going on. So, just being super appreciative of it.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron describes the emotional and unique experience of playing alongside his son, Bronny, in a meaningful playoff game, highlighting the personal significance of his continued career.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: There's not one team that's built, you know, eight, nine months of habits and then all of a sudden the playoffs start and they're like, up, we got to make adjustments, we got to scrap that and do something else. It's like, you know, you have your foundation and you're going to figure out ways how you can be better at things in the midst of what you've already done, you know. So how can we be better at what we already do? And and and those are like small little tweaks and and how and how many times can you do it over and over and over, you know, throughout the course of a playoff game, throughout the course of a series and you start to learn, you know, the person that you're playing against, the your opposition. You start to learn their tendencies. You start to see the flow of it. So, yeah, you know, there are some minor adjustments. Sometimes there's a lineup change. Sometimes there's a shift in defensively or how you play offensively, but you nobody's coming into a playoff series and saying, we're making an adjustment in game four and it's completely different from what we did the 82 games and the preseason and all the training like there's a foundation built over the course of the season.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron explains that playoff adjustments are not about completely changing a team's foundation but rather refining existing habits and understanding opponents' tendencies within their established system.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: It starts from the moment that we we arrive on that plane, you know, um, none of us wanted to get back on the plane to go to Houston. Um, we all wanted to close out at home and get some extra rest, especially my ass, you know. You know, I can use as many days as possible. Uh, so, you know, it starts from the moment that we're all walking on the plane. It's our demeanor when we get on the plane. It's how we feel about the moment, you know, and and not shying away from it. So, and it goes down, like you said, to the film sessions, to to whatever we're preparing for, you know, all the way up until, you know, the moment that the ball tips, you know, and that that that game. So, yeah, it it started, uh, way before we even got to Houston.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron details his comprehensive approach to leadership, emphasizing that motivation and preparation begin long before game time and extend through every aspect of the team's journey.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: I've never had to go through that and I can only imagine. Like, I I I did it from preseason to the regular season. I have so much more time to get back into game shape, you know, even with the regular season. But to have to to to be four or five weeks out and then have to jump back into a series, especially versus a Thompson twin and Houston and their physicality and their athleticism, you know, it's challenging. And, uh, you know, he came back in game five at home, gave us a spark offensively. Obviously, didn't shoot the ball well, but that just came from just I just didn't have any legs, you know, especially late in that game. And I mean, you know, it don't matter how much training, how much rehab and how much, you know, court work you're doing, there's no substitution for game, uh, fatigue, you know. So, but I thought in six, he did a great job of like attacking the paint, you know, just giving us that presence. We need another guy that can get in the paint and create the blender. And that's one guy that can do that. And and also, you know, he can get us into the bonus with his ability to, um, to create contact, create free throws and and fouls and things of that nature. So, it's just great to have him back, that's for sure. It gives us another presence.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron highlights the immense challenge of returning from a significant injury directly into playoff intensity, acknowledging the physical toll and the difficulty of regaining game shape without regular season ramp-up.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: No, no, actually I mean, it all happened by by fault, unfortunately. It's not saying that he never been able to do that, but when you lose so much in Luka and AR, we had to rely on Marcus and Luke, and at times Bronny, to create a blender. We needed to get into the paint, shift the defense from one side to the other. We noticed early on, even before the injuries, that Luke had that ability. Because his ability to shoot so well, a lot of teams run him off the line, but they don't realize he can also play in the blender, making plays for himself with pull-up jumpers and step-throughs, and spraying out for other guys to play against closeouts. When the injuries happened, we knew we was going to need more. We had no choice. He stepped up to the plate. I don't know if other teams utilized him as much in that position, but we've taken full advantage. I give a lot of credit to the coaching staff for empowering him, and all of us just told him, 'Hey, just stand on him. Do what you do. Be a ball player. You're not just a great shooter, the best shooter in our league percentage-wise, but a ball player too.' And he's taken that full responsibility.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron details how injuries to key players forced Luke Kennard into an expanded 'blender' role, showcasing his ability to create offense beyond just shooting, a facet of his game that other teams might have overlooked.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: Just about empowering DA, you know, um, you know, DA understanding he's the biggest, strongest, one of the most athletic guys on the on the court every night we hit the floor. Um, but empower him to, you know, rim run. We want to see, you know, look for him when he gets early rim runs and seals. He does an unbelievable job of setting screens and getting, you know, defenders off our bodies and and if teams are switching, you know, we want him to bury inside. And he's he's great in the pocket with that, you know, with that 12 to 15 mid-range shot. He's great in that. He's unbelievable. He had even in the game that we lost, I think it was game four against Houston, he had he had 10 offensive rebounds. Like, you know, he was such a present, um, presence in that game, um, even though we lost that game. It was either game four or game five. Maybe game five at home. He was just such a presence. Um, and we need that from him. We need his, um, his ability to, you know, like you said, block a shot or two, you know, but he also changed shots. We need him to have the ability to switch off on guards. Sometimes we go one through five where we switching, we feel like he has the lateral quickness, he has the the ability to guard some of our guards in our league and, um, he's been great for us, especially in the postseason.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron highlights Deandre Ayton's improved impact, emphasizing his physical dominance, screening ability, mid-range game, and defensive versatility, which have been crucial for the team's playoff success.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: Yeah, I think like we we just preached on, we understand like the the team that we were playing, like, and we know to take a little time to to get into the fight of it. And, you know, we had two main keys. It was protect the ball and block out. Like, you know, we were playing against a team in Houston who was the best offensive rebounding team in the last 25 years. You know, so, you know, when they miss shots, you know, they're getting second and third chances and it's just too hard, especially in the postseason to give teams multiple opportunities. And then if you're turning the ball over and you they're they're too fast, they're too athletic, they're too quick and you're giving them pick sixes. Um, and we saw, you know, what that what what can happen, you know, in that game five, you know, in that game four where we turned the ball over and and we didn't clean glass as much. So, um, they were very strategic and very on point about how we wanted to execute against Houston. Um, and yeah, so you know, throughout the course of a series, you make minor adjustments, but we had a staple on how we wanted to play and how we wanted to execute against them offensively, how we wanted to execute against them defensively. And, uh, we did a good job as far as the guys just kind of, you know, I want to say buying in because of course we're going to buy in. It's the postseason. But, um, guys understanding how we can get the best out of what they're giving us, the information that they're giving us in order to be able to accomplish the goal and that was to, you know, win a playoff series.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron praises the coaching staff's strategic game plan against Houston, emphasizing the focus on protecting the ball and defensive rebounding against a historically dominant offensive rebounding team, which ultimately led to their series victory.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: Boxing out, like that's one of the first, you know, drills that you do when you first start playing basketball. But, you know, you know, some of the things that gets lost in detail, it gets lost in the fundamentals of the game as we get bigger and stronger and faster and more athletic, you try to outleap everybody and you you lose some of those details. So we got back to that. Our first practice to begin the series, we literally started with a box-out drill. That was literally our first thing. And we didn't do a great job at it in game one and game two, but we got better and better and better as the series went on. And I think up to game all the way up until we played in game six, I think they only had seven offensive rebounds, you know, and we just was very detailed oriented, understanding our best possible chance for us to win is to control the controllables. And, uh, you know, and that's defensive cleaning glass. You're going to have some wild bounces where guys get offensive rebounds. You're going to have some where might have had any in your hand and, you know, got fumbled around. And then offensively, you're going to have some turnovers, but if there's turnovers out of aggression and not being passive, you can live with those.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron emphasizes the critical role of fundamental details like boxing out in playoff success, noting how returning to basics and improving execution throughout the series helped them control key aspects of the game.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: You know, I understand that at this point in my career that that's not probably going to be beneficial to the long-term of that game or, you know, even the next game, especially in the postseason of me running 10 straight pick and rolls or me having the ball in my hands for 10, 12 straight possessions. That's just not beneficial to not only myself, um, and then it won't be beneficial to the team. So, just kind of picking your spots, understanding like when the team may need this or need that. So playing off the ball, playing on the ball, you know, spotting up in the corner, just trying to defer, uh, you know, diversify my my portfolio all on the floor, you know, in order for me to have the maximum energy that I can produce still at this point in my career.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron discusses his strategic approach to energy management at 41, explaining how diversifying his offensive roles and picking his spots allows him to maximize his impact throughout games and series.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean, it's the same approach as as last series. I mean, we're we're undermanned and we're the underdog and we understand that, but it's even so you heighten that even more by like five, you know, because of, you know, their ability and what they bring to the table. They're one of the most historic basketball teams offensively and defensively that our league has seen. Um, and they got one of the most, you know, efficient players in our league history and and probably's going to be the MVP again. Um, you know, so we have to we we cannot shortcut the details, you know, in order for us to give ourself a chance to to to win games. We cannot shortcut the defe the details and the game plan. And we know we can't stop everything. It's impossible. They're they're that great. Um, but if we could control the controllables, which is another one of not turning the ball over because we know how great they are when it comes to pick sixes and how handsy they are and athleticism and speed that they play with, then, uh, you know, we can give ourself a chance. And that's all you can ask for in the postseason is a chance to compete and and and compete to win games.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron outlines his team's underdog mentality and strategic focus on controlling turnovers and adhering to the game plan against the historically great and efficient OKC Thunder, emphasizing the need for flawless execution to compete.
